residency.test: Resident if you have a permanent home available in Czechia, or stay at least 183 days in the calendar year.
residency.note: Days of presence are counted including days of arrival and departure.

headline.rates: 15% up to 36 times the average wage, 23% above
headline.capital_gains: 15% or 23%, with a time-test exemption for long-held securities

credits.name: Daňové zvýhodnění na dítě (child credit)
credits.note: 15,204 for the first child, 22,320 for the second, 27,840 for the third and later; refundable as a tax bonus

self_employed.name: Sociální pojištění OSVČ
self_employed.note: charged on 55% of profit in 2025, rising in steps to 60% by 2026

capital_gains.rate: taxed as other income at 15% or 23%
capital_gains.time_test: securities held more than three years, or shares in a company held more than five years, are exempt - but from 2025 the exemption is capped at 40m CZK of proceeds per year
capital_gains.real_estate: exempt after ten years of ownership, or five years for property acquired before 2021, or if the proceeds are used for your own housing needs
capital_gains.small_sales: annual securities sales under 100,000 CZK are exempt regardless of holding period

quirks: Most employees never file. If you have a single employer and sign the annual declaration (růžové prohlášení), payroll settles everything.
The three-year time test makes long-term securities investing effectively tax free for ordinary investors, subject to the new 40m cap from 2025.
The self-employed can use lump-sum expense percentages (paušální výdaje) of 40% to 80% of revenue depending on activity, with no receipts required - this is usually better than tracking real costs.
The paušální daň scheme lets small entrepreneurs pay one fixed monthly amount covering income tax, social and health, and file nothing at all.
Health insurance has no ceiling while social insurance does, so the marginal wedge falls at high income but never to zero.

reporting.who_must_file: Anyone with income from more than one employer at a time, self-employment income above 50,000 CZK, other income above 20,000 CZK, or income taxed at 23%. Single-employer employees who sign the annual declaration are settled by payroll.

documents_to_collect: Rodné číslo (birth number) and data box (datová schránka) or bank identity for electronic filing
Potvrzení o zdanitelných příjmech from each employer
Mortgage interest certificate - deductible up to 150,000 CZK
Pension and life insurance contribution confirmations
Broker statements including holding periods, which determine the time-test exemption

penalties.late_filing: 0.05% of the assessed tax per day, capped at 5% or 300,000 CZK; no penalty within a five working day grace period
penalties.late_payment: interest at the CNB repo rate plus 8 percentage points
penalties.failure_to_register: separate penalties for late registration as a taxpayer

warnings: The 23% rate applies to gross income above 36 times the average wage, not to taxable income after deductions - this model applies it to taxable income.
Lump-sum expense percentages and the paušální daň regime are not modelled and change the result substantially for the self-employed.
The spouse credit and disability credits are not included.
